It only inspects toy fixture files and exact copied-but-non-secret navigation source modules; it does not touch any live system. (ORGANS.md; classification_basis: "derived route-plane checks, source-coupling freshness, and public routing contract validation")

records.separating_case: No separating case found. The prose itself narrows the claim to toy fixtures and copied non-secret navigation source modules, explicitly disclaiming any live system contact, and the code matches exactly: the eight named negative cases (banned first-contact route, missing omission receipt, atlas-projection-as-control-entry, private-body leak, stale-freshness overclaim, duplicate route id, entry-payload field drop, undemoted anti-trigger passport) are each decided by a dedicated `validate_*` function keyed to fixture-declared fields (997-1181, 1291-1372), and `validate_source_module_manifest` (795-960) does a genuine `hashlib.sha256` recompute of each copied source-module file against its manifest-declared digest (862-880) plus a literal required-anchor substring scan (881-895) -- real file-level checks, not self-report. `validate_source_coupling_freshness` (960-994) recomputes a stable hash of `current_source_rows` and compares it to the fixture's own `rendered_source_sha256`, which is fixture-internal consistency, consistent with the prose's disclaimer that it does not establish live freshness.
records.notes: Several of the eight negative-case checks (route_card_boundary, atlas_projection_authority, summary_freshness) key off self-declared boolean flags in the fixture payload (e.g. `forbidden_content_value_present`, `claims_control_entry`) rather than independently re-deriving those properties from raw content. This is honestly scoped by the prose itself ('It only inspects toy fixture files...it does not touch any live system'), so it is not an overreach, but it is a weaker check-strength than the digest/hash-based checks in the same organ -- worth flagging per the protocol's falsification note about text_presence/self-report checks being weaker evidence than their description might imply on first read.

records.public_prose: This checks recorded examples of an agent finishing a piece of work the careful way: each example must name the exact files it claims to have touched, show that validation was recorded before any commit was attempted, and only label itself "committed" if the example also records the repository's HEAD moving. It also checks that blockers and ledger closeout were captured. The check shows whether each recorded work-claim carries the required evidence and ordering, rather than being an unbacked chat boast. It judges the recorded claims against the contract; it does not run Git or prove that any commit truly landed in a real repository. (ORGANS.md; classification_basis: "derived landing-lane checks for validation order, HEAD-advance claims, blockers, and scoped closeout evidence")

records.notes: This is a clean example of a claim that pre-emptively states its own limit in the main descriptive prose (not only in the separate claim_ceiling field), and the code delivers exactly that limited contract -- self-consistency of declared fields, not live Git verification.

records.separating_case: A reveal_walkthrough.json whose steps carry fabricated, non-existent evidence_refs/inspect_refs (e.g. four unique strings like 'totally_fake_receipt_1'..'_4' that name no real file) still passes validate_walkthrough (status=PASS at line 866 once len(steps)>=5, unique command_count>=4, unique evidence_count>=4) and validate_evidence_map (status=PASS at line 929 once evidence_id + ref + projection_not_authority are merely present). Neither function ever calls .is_file() or resolves an evidence_ref/inspect_ref against any file or receipt on disk -- unlike _source_module_manifest_result (404-566), which does open the target file and sha256-hash it, failing PUBLIC_REVEAL_SOURCE_MODULE_DIGEST_MISMATCH on a mismatch. Only the first half -- 'the declared route ... must still point to receipts' -- overclaims: it is a count-and-non-empty-string check (schema_shape), not a resolution check, even though the machinery to do real resolution (is_file + sha256) exists in the same file and is used for a different field. The registry's own classification_basis is more modest here and does not make the 'point to receipts' claim, so the gap is specifically in the ORGANS.md-level prose. Given the natural-language ambiguity of 'point to' (cite vs. resolve), confidence is medium rather than high.

records.separating_case: Separating case: build_public_prompt_injection_trace hardcodes every span's tool_name to the literal constant string 'prompt_injection_information_flow_policy' (src/microcosm_core/macro_tools/agent_execution_trace.py:1172), so _live_tool_call_trace_promotion's filter for 'a span with a tool_name' (line 1535) always matches the first flow row regardless of its content; the function then discards that span's real trust_label/verdict/taint fields entirely and substitutes a fixed template -- source.taint_labels=['prompt_injection','untrusted_tool_output'], flow.sanitization_applied=True, flow.privileged_sink=True, flow.policy_verdict='review' (lines 1558-1582) -- and runs that self-authored pair through _taint_propagation_receipt, which trivially reports a match because the 'declared' and 'derived' values were constructed identically. A fixture whose actual first flow is fully trusted, unprivileged, and carries no taint at all (e.g. source_trust_label='trusted_user_request', policy_verdict='allow') would still be 'promoted' and pass with the identical injected/reviewed labels, so the mechanic never actually derives taint from the generated trace's real content -- it only checks that its own canned substitute is self-consistent.
records.notes: The bulk of the organ (validate_information_flow_graph / _taint_propagation_receipt over the fixture-authored information_flows rows) IS a genuine recomputation: declared taint_labels and policy_verdict are compared against values independently derived from source trust labels, sink kind, privilege, and sanitization state, and a real mismatch (e.g. an author-declared verdict that disagrees with the derived one) is caught and blocks the run. The claim_above_check verdict applies specifically to the highlighted 'now promotes one generated public tool-call trace through the same taint-propagation mechanic' capability, which is the part of the classification_basis that most directly implies genuine content-driven propagation over live-generated input and is the part that turns out to be templated.
